authority: current owner intent + canonical doctrine/product specifications

active.decision: TypeScripture owns canonical engineering doctrine; context/docs and context/specs own Codependent Coding product-specific requirements; .agents/contracts are deterministic operational derivatives rather than a competing prose authority.
active.rationale: Preserves the paired-book doctrine boundary while giving product-specific specs explicit ownership.

active.decision: Codependent Coding is the WebApp Architecture. Loaded Vibes is the post-generation Codex enforcement/operations layer and is not the generator, materializer, or architecture identity.
active.rationale: Reconciles current product/generation specifications with legacy naming.

active.decision: The repository root is the public architecture/product/generator workspace. template/ is the single runnable Maximal Template superset application. Validators must not require template-only SaaS infrastructure from the public documentation/configuration site.
active.rationale: Prevents root-site and generated-application responsibilities from being conflated.

active.decision: Public architecture, Ontology, Simples, Anthimeria, Maximal Template, TypeScripture, and Loaded Vibes documentation surfaces are public by default. Identity becomes required only for future user/organization-owned persistent or private capabilities.

There is one Maximal Template, nine canonical Ontology defaults, and exactly two top-level Simples families: PureUI Blocks and BusinessLogic Blocks/Workflows. Ontologies normalize behavior; Anthimeria configures compatible presentation.
active.rationale: Prevents presets, constituent files, and UI controls from becoming parallel architectures.

active.decision: The dependency-closed Virgule is the single resolved materialization authority. Hipster Stack plans/materializes against real Maximal Template source into a standalone Arrangement.
active.rationale: Preserves the generation authority handoff and portability boundary.

active.decision: Anthimeria, CLI, and serialized configuration adapters share one normalization/validation/dependency-closure semantics model; no adapter may create hidden generation-relevant state.
active.rationale: Prevents UX or CLI adapters from becoming competing configuration authorities.

active.decision: Routes adapt; Features orchestrate; Components render; Fetchers read; Actions write; Schemas validate; Authorization decides; Workflows coordinate use cases; Transactions preserve invariants; integrations own provider mechanics; webhooks reconcile external truth.

Features may compose compatible UI Primitives as well as PureUI Blocks. The older Loaded Vibes block-only Feature import rule is superseded; DB/provider/server authority remains forbidden in Features.
active.rationale: Reconciles current TypeScripture and product technical requirements.

active.decision: New domain-owned workflow placement follows lib/<domain>/workflows. The existing template/lib/workflows/<domain> layout is transitional evidence and should be migrated only through a scoped import-safe change, not an automatic blind move.
active.rationale: Newest TypeScripture realization is more recent than the older Loaded Vibes placement while the current template still requires compatibility.

active.decision: Protected authorization is server-determined; tenant-owned rows use explicit tenant predicates plus transaction-local PostgreSQL RLS under restricted runtime credentials. Client IDs/roles/prices/provider identifiers do not establish authority.
active.rationale: Combines TypeScripture auth/authz/RLS doctrine with current public-site trust boundaries.

active.decision: packages/loaded-vibes is the canonical package source. .agents/LoadedVibesCodexPlugin/loaded-vibes is a non-authoritative managed mirror and must remain byte-identical when present.
active.rationale: Keeps the requested agent-local package available without allowing duplicate source authority drift.

active.decision: Repository governance uses contract-driven mechanical validators and conservative fixers. They enforce only properties static inspection can prove and explicitly label semantic/runtime obligations as review or runtime evidence.
active.rationale: Avoids both unenforced architecture and fake omniscient validators.

active.decision: The old segmented consolidation/deployment execution records are historical. Current .agents/execution files describe the present governance-contract consolidation and subsequent handoff only.
active.rationale: Execution state is temporary evidence, not a museum exhibit with write permissions.

active.decision: The .yaml contracts use the YAML 1.2 JSON-compatible subset so repository-owned Node scripts can parse them with JSON.parse and no additional YAML runtime dependency.
active.rationale: Keeps machine contracts deterministic, dependency-free, and valid YAML.

history.decision: Loaded Vibes is optimized for developer time saved and the usefulness of the generated repository, not governance breadth.
CLI, web configurator, and loadedvibes.json share one configuration schema and normalization path.

Loaded Vibes is the sole executable application-template authority and DevNotes is the Hipster Stack doctrine authority. DigitalHerencia/Vibes is not an upstream, reference, sync, provenance, packaging, or runtime dependency.
The final repository contains one maximal white-label application at template/. Generation copies that source, resolves ownership, removes excluded material, and applies structured transforms.

packages/recipes and duplicated templates/modules source are migration-era structures. Useful defaults and ownership semantics may be preserved, but the structures themselves are not the target architecture.
Presets, when retained, are convenience defaults over one configuration model and never represent separate templates or architectures.
A configuration option is user-selectable only when Loaded Vibes can make a real deterministic change to generated output or project lifecycle.
Loaded Vibes' website is a dark developer tool with separate landing, configure, and docs surfaces. The CLI remains the primary execution surface and the web configurator remains stateless.
Root docs/ is the canonical end-user documentation source. context/ remains maintainer/Codex context.
The migration adds no new tests or validation systems. Existing relevant checks may be run proportionally for the behavior changed by an Issue.

The LV-201 through LV-207 migration is complete. The final repository owns one template at template/, packages cli/core/schema, shared configuration semantics, the canonical loaded-vibes command, stateless web routes, and canonical end-user docs at docs/.

The owner-approved 2026-08-13 Constituter redesign supersedes older fixed-composition governance: architecture remains opinionated while providers, capabilities, authorization, routes, resources, and safe output policy move behind one canonical Application Definition and resolver. The web workbench is named The Constituter™.

The 2026-08-28 handoff authority establishes TypeScripture as doctrine, Codependent Coding as the Web App Architecture, Hipster Stack as the resolver/generator/CLI technology, Anthimeria as the stateless workbench, Virgule as the dependency-closed definition, Arrangement as generated output, and Loaded Vibes as post-generation Codex operations.

Nine Ontology normalized defaults replace the four generic presets as canonical starters; Simples contains only PureUI Blocks and BusinessLogic Blocks or Workflows; one shared resolver remains authoritative for CLI, config, Anthimeria preview, planning, and materialization.

The consolidation workspace is local implementation evidence, not a repository identity. Remote creation, push, publication, deployment, and credential provisioning remain deferred until owner acceptance.

Owner acceptance on 2026-08-28 authorized publication of the completed consolidation build to DigitalHerencia/CodependentCoding and production deployment through the existing digital-herencia/codependent-coding Vercel project at codependentcoding.vercel.app.
